parts.title: Incipit Epístola cathólica beáti Judæ Apóstoli

verses.text: Judas, Jesu Christi servus, frater autem Jacóbi, his qui sunt in Deo Patre diléctis, et Christo Jesu conservátis, et vocátis.
Misericórdia vobis, et pax, et cáritas adimpleátur.
Caríssimi, omnem sollicitúdinem fáciens scribéndi vobis de commúni vestra salúte, necésse hábui scríbere vobis: déprecans supercertári semel tráditæ sanctis fídei.
Subintroiérunt enim quidam hómines (qui olim præscrípti sunt in hoc judícium) ímpii, Dei nostri grátiam transferéntes in luxúriam, et solum Dominatórem, et Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum negántes.

responsory.text: Ecce ego mitto vos sicut oves in médio lupórum, dicit Dóminus:
responsory.repeat: Estóte ergo prudéntes sicut serpéntes, et símplices sicut colúmbæ.

responsory.text: Tradent enim vos in concíliis, et in synagógis suis flagellábunt vos.
Estóte ergo prudéntes sicut serpéntes, et símplices sicut colúmbæ.

parts.title: Beginning of the letter of the blessed Apostle Jude

verses.text: Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James: to them that are beloved in God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ, and called.
Mercy unto you, and peace, and charity be fulfilled.

Dearly beloved, taking all care to write unto you concerning your common salvation, I was under a necessity to write unto you: to beseech you to contend earnestly for the faith once delivered to the saints.

For certain men are secretly entered in, (who were written of long ago unto this judgment,) ungodly men, turning the grace of our Lord God into riotousness, and denying the only sovereign Ruler, and our Lord Jesus Christ.

responsory.text: Behold, I send you as sheep in the midst of wolves, said the Lord:
responsory.repeat: Be ye, therefore, wise as serpents and simple as doves.

responsory.text: For they shall deliver you up to councils: and in the synagogues you shall be beaten: and you shall stand before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony unto them.
Be ye, therefore, wise as serpents and simple as doves.

verses.text: Commonére autem vos volo, sciéntes semel ómnia, quóniam Jesus pópulum de terra Ægýpti salvans, secúndo eos, qui non credidérunt, pérdidit:
Ángelos vero, qui non servavérunt suum principátum, sed dereliquérunt suum domicílium, in judícium magni diéi, vínculis ætérnis sub calígine reservávit.
Sicut Sódoma, et Gomórrha, et finítimæ civitátes símili modo exfornicátæ, et abeúntes post carnem álteram, factæ sunt exémplum, ignis ætérni pœnam sustinéntes.
Simíliter et hi carnem quidem máculant, dominatiónem autem spernunt, majestátem autem blasphémant.

responsory.text: Tóllite jugum meum super vos, dicit Dóminus, et díscite a me, quia mitis sum et húmilis corde:
responsory.repeat: Jugum enim meum suáve est, et onus meum leve.

responsory.text: Et inveniétis réquiem animábus vestris.
Jugum enim meum suáve est, et onus meum leve.

verses.text: I will therefore admonish you, though ye once knew all things, that Jesus, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, did afterwards destroy them that believed not:
And the angels who kept not their principality, but forsook their own habitation, he hath reserved under darkness in everlasting chains, unto the judgment of the great day.

As Sodom and Gomorrha, and the neighbouring cities, in like manner, having given themselves to fornication, and going after other flesh, were made an example, suffering the punishment of eternal fire.
In like manner these men also defile the flesh, and despise dominion, and blaspheme majesty.

responsory.text: Take up my yoke upon you, said the Lord, and learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart.
responsory.repeat: For my yoke is sweet and my burden light.

responsory.text: And you shall find rest to your souls.
For my yoke is sweet and my burden light.

verses.text: Cum Míchael Archángelus cum diábolo dísputans altercarétur de Móysi córpore, non est ausus judícium inférre blasphémiæ: sed dixit: Imperet tibi Dóminus.
Hi autem quæcúmque quidem ignórant, blasphémant: quæcúmque autem naturáliter, tamquam muta animália, norunt, in his corrumpúntur.
Væ illis, quia in via Cain abiérunt, et erróre Bálaam mercéde effúsi sunt, et in contradictióne Core periérunt!

responsory.text: Dum stetéritis ante reges et prǽsides, nolíte cogitáre quómodo aut quid loquámini:
responsory.repeat: Dábitur enim vobis in illa hora, quid loquámini.

responsory.text: Non enim vos estis qui loquímini: sed Spíritus Patris vestri, qui lóquitur in vobis.
Dábitur enim vobis in illa hora, quid loquámini.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Dábitur enim vobis in illa hora, quid loquámini.

verses.text: When Michael the archangel, disputing with the devil, contended about the body of Moses, he durst not bring against him the judgment of railing speech, but said: The Lord command thee.
But these men blaspheme whatever things they know not: and what things soever they naturally know, like dumb beasts, in these they are corrupted.
Woe unto them, for they have gone in the way of Cain: and after the error of Balaam they have for reward poured out themselves, and have perished in the contradiction of Core.

responsory.text: But when they shall deliver you up to the judges, take no thought how or what to speak:
responsory.repeat: for it shall be given you in that hour what to speak:

responsory.text: For it is not you that speak, but the spirit of your Father that speaketh in you.
For it shall be given you in that hour what to speak.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
For it shall be given you in that hour what to speak.

paragraphs: Simon Chananǽus, qui et Zelótes, et Thaddǽus, qui et Judas Jacóbi appellátur in Evangélio, uníus ex cathólicis Epístolis scriptor; hic Mesopotámiam, ille Ægýptum evangélica prædicatióne peragrávit. Póstea in Pérsidem conveniéntes, cum innumerábiles fílios Jesu Christo peperíssent fidémque in vastíssimis illis regiónibus et efferátis géntibus disseminássent, doctrína et miráculis, ac dénique glorióso martýrio, simul sanctíssimum Jesu Christi nomen illustrárunt.

responsory.text: Vidi conjúnctos viros, habéntes spléndidas vestes, et Ángelus Dómini locútus est ad me, dicens:
responsory.repeat: Isti sunt viri sancti facti amíci Dei.

responsory.text: Vidi Ángelum Dei fortem, volántem per médium cælum, voce magna clamántem et dicéntem.
Isti sunt viri sancti facti amíci Dei.

paragraphs: Simon the Canaanite, called also Zelotes, went through Egypt preaching the Gospel, whileas the like was done in Mesopotamia by Thaddaeus, called also in the Gospel Judas the brother of James, and the writer of one of the Catholic Epistles. They met together afterwards in Persia, where they begat countless children in Jesus Christ, spread the faith far and wide in those lands, amid raging heathens, and glorified together by their teaching and miracles, and, in the end, by a glorious martyrdom, the most holy name of Jesus Christ.

responsory.text: I saw men standing together, clad in shining raiment, and the Angel of the Lord spoke unto me, saying:
responsory.repeat: These men are holy, for they are the friends of God.

responsory.text: I saw a strong Angel of God fly into the midst of heaven, saying with a loud voice:
These men are holy, for they are the friends of God.

parts.title: Sermo sancti Gregórii Papæ
paragraphs: Scriptum est: Spíritus Dómini ornávit cælos. Ornaménta enim cælórum sunt virtútes prædicántium. Quæ vidélicet ornaménta Paulus enúmerat, dicens: Álii datur per Spíritum sermo sapiéntiæ, álii sermo sciéntiæ secúndum eúndem Spíritum, álteri fides in eódem Spíritu, álii grátia sanitátum in uno Spíritu, álii operátio virtútum, álii prophetía, álii discrétio spirítuum, álii génera linguárum, álii interpretátio sermónum. Hæc autem ómnia operátur unus atque idem Spíritus, dívidens síngulis prout vult.

responsory.text: Isti sunt triumphatóres et amíci Dei, qui contemnéntes jussa príncipum, meruérunt prǽmia ætérna:
Isti sunt qui venérunt ex magna tribulatióne, et lavérunt stolas suas in sánguine Agni.
Modo coronántur, et accípiunt palmam.

parts.title: Sermon of St. Gregory, Pope
paragraphs: It is written: By His Spirit the Lord hath adorned the heavens. (Job xxvi. 13.) Now the ornament of the heavens are the godly powers of preachers, and this ornament, what it is, Paul teacheth us thus To one is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom, to another the word of knowledge by the same Spirit; to another faith by the same Spirit; to another the gifts of healing by the same Spirit, to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another discerning of spirits, to another diverse kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues. But all these worketh that one and the self-same Spirit, dividing to every man severally as He will. (1 Cor. xii. 8.)

responsory.text: These are they which have conquered, and are become the friends of God, who recked not of the commandments of princes, and earned the everlasting reward.
responsory.repeat: And now have they crowns on their heads, and palms in their hands.

responsory.text: These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb.
And now have they crowns on their heads, and palms in their hands.

paragraphs: Quot ergo sunt bona prædicántium, tot sunt ornaménta cælórum. Hinc rursus scriptum est: Verbo Dómini cæli firmáti sunt. Verbum enim Dómini Fílius est Patris. Sed eósdem cælos, vidélicet sanctos Apóstolos, ut tota simul sancta Trínitas ostendátur operáta, repénte de Sancti Spíritus divinitáte adjúngitur: Et Spíritu oris ejus omnis virtus eórum. Cælórum ergo virtus de Spíritu sumpta est: quia mundi hujus potestátibus contraíre non præsúmerent, nisi eos Sancti Spíritus fortitúdo solidásset. Quales namque doctóres sanctæ Ecclésiæ ante advéntum hujus Spíritus fúerint, scimus: et post advéntum illíus, cujus fortitúdinis facti sint, conspícimus.

responsory.text: Vos estis lux mundi, dicit Dóminus:
responsory.repeat: Qui in patiéntia vestra possidébitis ánimas vestras.

responsory.text: Et ego dispóno vobis, sicut dispósuit mihi Pater meus regnum, ut edátis, et bibátis super mensam meam in regno meo.
Qui in patiéntia vestra possidébitis ánimas vestras.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Possidébitis ánimas vestras.

paragraphs: So much power then as have preachers, so much ornament have the heavens. Wherefore again it is written By the word of the Lord were the heavens made. ~(Ps. xxxii. 6.) For the Word of the Lord is the Son of the Father. But, to the end that all the Holy Trinity may be made manifest as the Maker of the heavens, that is, of the Apostles, it is straightway added touching God the Holy Ghost: you and all the host of them by the Breath of His mouth. Therefore the might of the same heavens is the might of the Spirit, for they had not braved the powers of this world, unless the strength of the Holy Ghost had comforted them. For we know what manner of men the Teachers of the Holy Church were before the coming of this Spirit and since He came we see in Whose strength they are made strong.

responsory.text: Vos estis lux mundi, dicit Dóminus:
responsory.repeat: Qui in patiéntia vestra possidébitis ánimas vestras.

responsory.text: Et ego dispóno vobis, sicut dispósuit mihi Pater meus regnum, ut edátis, et bibátis super mensam meam in regno meo.
Qui in patiéntia vestra possidébitis ánimas vestras.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
Possidébitis ánimas vestras.

parts.title: Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Joánnem
paragraphs: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis: Hæc mando vobis, ut diligátis ínvicem. Si mundus vos odit, scitóte quia me priórem vobis ódio hábuit. Et réliqua.

parts.title: Homilía sancti Cyrílli Epíscopi Alexandríni
parts.source: Lib. 10 in Joann. cap. 26 et seq.
paragraphs: Mirábili quodam atque divíno in conformándis firmandísque discipulórum ánimis Dóminus útitur artifício. Nam quóniam totíus orbis terrárum doctóres futúri erant, quos ubíque omnes quasi Evangélii legem ac régulam imitaréntur, necessário nullam curam iis faciéndam esse monet, ne a mundo, id est ab homínibus voluptáti impietatíque déditis, ódio habeántur. Cum ergo, inquit, mundi ódium vobis opponétur, non turbabímini, si hoc mihi ipsi, qui sum Dóminus, accidísse meminéritis.

responsory.text: Isti sunt viri sancti, quos elégit Dóminus in caritáte non ficta, et dedit illis glóriam sempitérnam:
responsory.repeat: Quorum doctrína fulget Ecclésia, ut sole luna.

responsory.text: In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum, et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
Quorum doctrína fulget Ecclésia, ut sole luna.

parts.title: From the holy Gospel according to John
paragraphs: at that time, Jesus said to his disciples: These things I command you, that you love one another. If the world hate you, know ye, that it hath hated me before you. And so on.

responsory.repeat: By the light of whose teaching the Church is glorified, even as the moon is glorified by the light of the sun.

responsory.text: Their sound is gone out through all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.
By the light of whose teaching the Church is glorified, even as the moon is glorified by the light of the sun.

paragraphs: Quia de mundo non estis, sed ego elégi vos de mundo, proptérea odit vos mundus. Fácile, immo vero jucúndum esse osténdit, quod natúra sui molestíssimum est. Quid enim acérbius et plerúmque damnósius quam ódio habéri? Suáve tamen id effícitur propter Deum. Et quando grátia pietátis áccidit, arguménto est, non inhiáre rebus cadúcis eum qui ódio habétur. Ut enim córporum, ita morum cognátio quædam est, quorum similitúdo longe sánguinis vincit cognatiónem.

responsory.text: Qui sunt isti, qui ut nubes volant,
responsory.repeat: Et quasi colúmbæ ad fenéstras suas?

responsory.text: Candidióres nive, nitidióres lacte, rubicundióres ébore antíquo.
Et quasi colúmbæ ad fenéstras suas?

responsory.text: Who are these, that fly as clouds,
responsory.repeat: And as doves to their windows?

responsory.text: They are purer than snow, they are whiter than milk, they are more ruddy in body than coral, their polishing is of sapphire.
And as doves to their windows?

paragraphs: Sanctus cum sancto, et pervérsus cum pervérso jucúnde conversátur. Quam ob rem necésse est ut studiósus mínime a vitiósis diligátur: unde non doléndum, sed gaudéndum pótius nobis Christus esse ásserit. Nam etsi detriméntum in rebus cadúcis multórum ódium áfferat, máximo tamen apud Deum est emoluménto. Effícitur autem his verbis, ut líbere et absque ódii formídine discípuli prædicatióne utántur: cum nihil dilectióni Dei præponéndum esse doceántur.

email.html:
Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James: to them that are beloved in God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ, and call…

Matins · Wednesday, 28 October 2026

Sts. Simon and Jude, Apostles

Ss. Simonis et Judæ Apostolorum · Duplex II classis

Read in Latin and English

Lesson I

Beginning of the letter of the blessed Apostle Jude

Jude 1:1-4

Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James: to them that are beloved in God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ, and called. Mercy unto you, and peace, and charity be fulfilled. Dearly beloved, taking all care to write unto you concerning your common salvation, I was under a necessity to write unto you: to beseech you to contend earnestly for the faith once delivered to the saints. For certain men are secretly entered in, (who were written of long ago unto this judgment,) ungodly men, turning the grace of our Lord God into riotousness, and denying the only sovereign Ruler, and our Lord Jesus Christ.

℟. Behold, I send you as sheep in the midst of wolves, said the Lord: * Be ye, therefore, wise as serpents and simple as doves.

℟. For they shall deliver you up to councils: and in the synagogues you shall be beaten: and you shall stand before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony unto them.

℟. Be ye, therefore, wise as serpents and simple as doves.

Lesson II

Jude 1:5-8

I will therefore admonish you, though ye once knew all things, that Jesus, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, did afterwards destroy them that believed not: And the angels who kept not their principality, but forsook their own habitation, he hath reserved under darkness in everlasting chains, unto the judgment of the great day. As Sodom and Gomorrha, and the neighbouring cities, in like manner, having given themselves to fornication, and going after other flesh, were made an example, suffering the punishment of eternal fire. In like manner these men also defile the flesh, and despise dominion, and blaspheme majesty.

℟. Take up my yoke upon you, said the Lord, and learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart. * For my yoke is sweet and my burden light.

℣. And you shall find rest to your souls.

℟. For my yoke is sweet and my burden light.

Lesson III

Jude 1:9-13

When Michael the archangel, disputing with the devil, contended about the body of Moses, he durst not bring against him the judgment of railing speech, but said: The Lord command thee. But these men blaspheme whatever things they know not: and what things soever they naturally know, like dumb beasts, in these they are corrupted. Woe unto them, for they have gone in the way of Cain: and after the error of Balaam they have for reward poured out themselves, and have perished in the contradiction of Core.

℟. But when they shall deliver you up to the judges, take no thought how or what to speak: * for it shall be given you in that hour what to speak:

℣. For it is not you that speak, but the spirit of your Father that speaketh in you.

℟. For it shall be given you in that hour what to speak.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. For it shall be given you in that hour what to speak.

Lesson IV

Simon the Canaanite, called also Zelotes, went through Egypt preaching the Gospel, whileas the like was done in Mesopotamia by Thaddaeus, called also in the Gospel Judas the brother of James, and the writer of one of the Catholic Epistles. They met together afterwards in Persia, where they begat countless children in Jesus Christ, spread the faith far and wide in those lands, amid raging heathens, and glorified together by their teaching and miracles, and, in the end, by a glorious martyrdom, the most holy name of Jesus Christ.

℟. I saw men standing together, clad in shining raiment, and the Angel of the Lord spoke unto me, saying: * These men are holy, for they are the friends of God.

℣. I saw a strong Angel of God fly into the midst of heaven, saying with a loud voice:

℟. These men are holy, for they are the friends of God.

Lesson V

Sermon of St. Gregory, Pope

Sermon 30 on the Gospels

It is written: By His Spirit the Lord hath adorned the heavens. (Job xxvi. 13.) Now the ornament of the heavens are the godly powers of preachers, and this ornament, what it is, Paul teacheth us thus To one is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom, to another the word of knowledge by the same Spirit; to another faith by the same Spirit; to another the gifts of healing by the same Spirit, to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another discerning of spirits, to another diverse kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues. But all these worketh that one and the self-same Spirit, dividing to every man severally as He will. (1 Cor. xii. 8.)

℟. These are they which have conquered, and are become the friends of God, who recked not of the commandments of princes, and earned the everlasting reward. * And now have they crowns on their heads, and palms in their hands.

℣. These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb.

℟. And now have they crowns on their heads, and palms in their hands.

Lesson VI

So much power then as have preachers, so much ornament have the heavens. Wherefore again it is written By the word of the Lord were the heavens made. ~(Ps. xxxii. 6.) For the Word of the Lord is the Son of the Father. But, to the end that all the Holy Trinity may be made manifest as the Maker of the heavens, that is, of the Apostles, it is straightway added touching God the Holy Ghost: you and all the host of them by the Breath of His mouth. Therefore the might of the same heavens is the might of the Spirit, for they had not braved the powers of this world, unless the strength of the Holy Ghost had comforted them. For we know what manner of men the Teachers of the Holy Church were before the coming of this Spirit and since He came we see in Whose strength they are made strong.

℟. Vos estis lux mundi, dicit Dóminus: * Qui in patiéntia vestra possidébitis ánimas vestras.

℣. Et ego dispóno vobis, sicut dispósuit mihi Pater meus regnum, ut edátis, et bibátis super mensam meam in regno meo.

℟. Qui in patiéntia vestra possidébitis ánimas vestras.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Possidébitis ánimas vestras.

Lesson VII

From the holy Gospel according to John

John 15:17-25

at that time, Jesus said to his disciples: These things I command you, that you love one another. If the world hate you, know ye, that it hath hated me before you. And so on.

Homilía sancti Cyrílli Epíscopi Alexandríni

Mirábili quodam atque divíno in conformándis firmandísque discipulórum ánimis Dóminus útitur artifício. Nam quóniam totíus orbis terrárum doctóres futúri erant, quos ubíque omnes quasi Evangélii legem ac régulam imitaréntur, necessário nullam curam iis faciéndam esse monet, ne a mundo, id est ab homínibus voluptáti impietatíque déditis, ódio habeántur. Cum ergo, inquit, mundi ódium vobis opponétur, non turbabímini, si hoc mihi ipsi, qui sum Dóminus, accidísse meminéritis.

℟. These men are saints, whom the Lord hath chosen in love unfeigned, and hath given them glory everlasting. These are they * By the light of whose teaching the Church is glorified, even as the moon is glorified by the light of the sun.

℣. Their sound is gone out through all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.

℟. By the light of whose teaching the Church is glorified, even as the moon is glorified by the light of the sun.

Lesson VIII

Quia de mundo non estis, sed ego elégi vos de mundo, proptérea odit vos mundus. Fácile, immo vero jucúndum esse osténdit, quod natúra sui molestíssimum est. Quid enim acérbius et plerúmque damnósius quam ódio habéri? Suáve tamen id effícitur propter Deum. Et quando grátia pietátis áccidit, arguménto est, non inhiáre rebus cadúcis eum qui ódio habétur. Ut enim córporum, ita morum cognátio quædam est, quorum similitúdo longe sánguinis vincit cognatiónem.

℟. Who are these, that fly as clouds, * And as doves to their windows?

℣. They are purer than snow, they are whiter than milk, they are more ruddy in body than coral, their polishing is of sapphire.

℟. And as doves to their windows?

Lesson I
Beginning of the letter of the blessed Apostle Jude

Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James: to them that are beloved in God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ, and called. Mercy unto you, and peace, and charity be fulfilled. Dearly beloved, taking all care to write unto you concerning your common salvation, I was under a necessity to write unto you: to beseech you to contend earnestly for the faith once delivered to the saints. For certain men are secretly entered in, (who were written of long ago unto this judgment,) ungodly men, turning the grace of our Lord God into riotousness, and denying the only sovereign Ruler, and our Lord Jesus Christ.

℟. Behold, I send you as sheep in the midst of wolves, said the Lord: * Be ye, therefore, wise as serpents and simple as doves.
℟. For they shall deliver you up to councils: and in the synagogues you shall be beaten: and you shall stand before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony unto them.
℟. Be ye, therefore, wise as serpents and simple as doves.

Lesson II
Jude 1:5-8
I will therefore admonish you, though ye once knew all things, that Jesus, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, did afterwards destroy them that believed not: And the angels who kept not their principality, but forsook their own habitation, he hath reserved under darkness in everlasting chains, unto the judgment of the great day. As Sodom and Gomorrha, and the neighbouring cities, in like manner, having given themselves to fornication, and going after other flesh, were made an example, suffering the punishment of eternal fire. In like manner these men also defile the flesh, and despise dominion, and blaspheme majesty.

℟. Take up my yoke upon you, said the Lord, and learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart. * For my yoke is sweet and my burden light.
℣. And you shall find rest to your souls.
℟. For my yoke is sweet and my burden light.

Lesson III
Jude 1:9-13
When Michael the archangel, disputing with the devil, contended about the body of Moses, he durst not bring against him the judgment of railing speech, but said: The Lord command thee. But these men blaspheme whatever things they know not: and what things soever they naturally know, like dumb beasts, in these they are corrupted. Woe unto them, for they have gone in the way of Cain: and after the error of Balaam they have for reward poured out themselves, and have perished in the contradiction of Core.

℟. But when they shall deliver you up to the judges, take no thought how or what to speak: * for it shall be given you in that hour what to speak:
℣. For it is not you that speak, but the spirit of your Father that speaketh in you.
℟. For it shall be given you in that hour what to speak.
℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. For it shall be given you in that hour what to speak.

Lesson IV
Simon the Canaanite, called also Zelotes, went through Egypt preaching the Gospel, whileas the like was done in Mesopotamia by Thaddaeus, called also in the Gospel Judas the brother of James, and the writer of one of the Catholic Epistles. They met together afterwards in Persia, where they begat countless children in Jesus Christ, spread the faith far and wide in those lands, amid raging heathens, and glorified together by their teaching and miracles, and, in the end, by a glorious martyrdom, the most holy name of Jesus Christ.

℟. I saw men standing together, clad in shining raiment, and the Angel of the Lord spoke unto me, saying: * These men are holy, for they are the friends of God.
℣. I saw a strong Angel of God fly into the midst of heaven, saying with a loud voice:
℟. These men are holy, for they are the friends of God.

Lesson V
Sermon of St. Gregory, Pope
Sermon 30 on the Gospels
It is written: By His Spirit the Lord hath adorned the heavens. (Job xxvi. 13.) Now the ornament of the heavens are the godly powers of preachers, and this ornament, what it is, Paul teacheth us thus To one is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom, to another the word of knowledge by the same Spirit; to another faith by the same Spirit; to another the gifts of healing by the same Spirit, to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another discerning of spirits, to another diverse kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues. But all these worketh that one and the self-same Spirit, dividing to every man severally as He will. (1 Cor. xii. 8.)

℟. These are they which have conquered, and are become the friends of God, who recked not of the commandments of princes, and earned the everlasting reward. * And now have they crowns on their heads, and palms in their hands.
℣. These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb.
℟. And now have they crowns on their heads, and palms in their hands.

So much power then as have preachers, so much ornament have the heavens. Wherefore again it is written By the word of the Lord were the heavens made. ~(Ps. xxxii. 6.) For the Word of the Lord is the Son of the Father. But, to the end that all the Holy Trinity may be made manifest as the Maker of the heavens, that is, of the Apostles, it is straightway added touching God the Holy Ghost: you and all the host of them by the Breath of His mouth. ℟. Qui in patiéntia vestra possidébitis ánimas vestras.
℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. Possidébitis ánimas vestras.

From the holy Gospel according to John
John 15:17-25
at that time, Jesus said to his disciples: These things I command you, that you love one another. If the world hate you, know ye, that it hath hated me before you. And so on.

Incipit Epístola cathólica beáti Judæ Apóstoli

Jude 1:1-4

Judas, Jesu Christi servus, frater autem Jacóbi, his qui sunt in Deo Patre diléctis, et Christo Jesu conservátis, et vocátis. Misericórdia vobis, et pax, et cáritas adimpleátur. Caríssimi, omnem sollicitúdinem fáciens scribéndi vobis de commúni vestra salúte, necésse hábui scríbere vobis: déprecans supercertári semel tráditæ sanctis fídei. Subintroiérunt enim quidam hómines (qui olim præscrípti sunt in hoc judícium) ímpii, Dei nostri grátiam transferéntes in luxúriam, et solum Dominatórem, et Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum negántes.

For certain men are secretly entered in, (who were written of long ago unto this judgment,) ungodly men, turning the grace of our Lord God into riotousness, and denying the only sovereign Ruler, and our Lord Jesus Christ.

Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Joánnem

From the holy Gospel according to John

John 15:17-25
